# grub

**A ridiculously simple search engine factory.**

Point `grub` at *anything* — a folder, a codebase, a Python package, a
website, a pile of notes — and get back a working search engine in one
line. No servers, no indexes to babysit, no configuration.

```bash
pip install grub
```

```python
from grub import grub

grub("./my_notes", "where did I write about retirement savings")
```

---

## The AI-first way (start here)

You probably shouldn’t be calling `grub` yourself at all.

grub ships with **agent skills** — instruction files that teach an AI
coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, and friends) how to drive grub on your
behalf. The skills live in [`.claude/skills/`]():

| Skill             | What it lets the agent do                                                                                           |
|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **`grub-search`** | Build a search index over a folder, codebase, module, website, or list of strings, and answer questions against it. |
| **`grub-extend`** | Wire grub up to custom embedding providers (OpenAI, Cohere, …), new backends, or new data sources.                  |

With the skills in place, you stop writing code and start *asking*:

> “Search my `./docs` folder and tell me which file explains the
> deployment process.”
> “Index this codebase and find where rate limiting is implemented.”
> “Use semantic search over my meeting notes to find anything about the
> Q3 budget.”
> “Search these three documentation URLs and summarize what they say
> about authentication.”

The agent reads the skill, picks the right source type, the right search
method (lexical, semantic, or hybrid), chunks long documents when it
helps, and hands you the answer. You never see a `SearchStore`
constructor. You never tune a vectorizer. You describe the outcome you
want, in English, and it happens.

### Why AI-first?

Because the interface to software is changing, and grub is built for the
change.

For decades, “using a tool” meant *learning the tool* — its API, its
flags, its mental model — and then translating your intent into its
vocabulary. That translation tax was unavoidable. It is not anymore.

An AI agent is a universal adapter between human intent and machine
capability. It already knows grub’s vocabulary; you don’t have to. So the
job of a well-designed library is no longer “expose a clever API to
humans” — it’s **“expose powerful, composable capabilities, and ship the
knowledge an agent needs to wield them.”** That knowledge is the skill
files.

grub leans all the way into this:

- **The skills are the primary interface.** They are documentation an
  agent *executes*, not documentation a human *reads and then forgets*.
- **The Python API is the substrate.** It stays clean, small, and
  honest — because an agent calling it deserves the same good design a
  human would.
- **You operate at the level of intent.** “Find the doc about X” instead
  of “instantiate, configure, fit, query, parse.”

The future of tooling is not humans memorizing more APIs. It’s humans
stating goals and agents composing capabilities. grub is a small tool, so
it’s a small example — but the shape is the same all the way up.

---

## For the dinosaurs who want to operate with code directly 🦖

No judgment. Sometimes you *are* the agent, and a REPL is the fastest
path. The Python API is built to be a pleasure to use directly.

### One function does it all

```python
from grub import grub

search = grub("./docs")  # build a searcher
results = grub("./docs", "how to deploy")  # ...or search in one call
```

`grub()` figures out what you handed it:

```python
grub("./docs")  # a folder of files
grub("src/**/*.py")  # a glob
grub(some_module)  # a Python package's source
grub("https://example.com/guide")  # a web page (HTML stripped to text)
grub({"intro": "...", "faq": "..."})  # a dict of documents
grub(["first doc", "second doc"])  # a list of strings
```

### Results that explain themselves

```python
results = grub("./docs", "configure logging")

for hit in results:
    print(hit.score, hit.key, hit.snippet)

results.keys  # ['logging.md', 'setup.md', ...]  best-first
results.scores  # [0.71, 0.33, ...]
print(results.show())  # a tidy ranked rendering
print(search["logging.md"])  # the full original text of a hit
```

Every hit carries a **score** and a **snippet** — the line that shows you
*why* it matched.

### Three ways to search

```python
grub(src, query, method="tfidf")  # lexical: shared words (default, fast)
grub(src, query, method="semantic")  # embeddings: shared *meaning*
grub(src, query, method="hybrid")  # a blend of both
```

Semantic search finds “automobile” when you searched “car”. It needs
embeddings — either `pip install 'grub[semantic]'` (a local
sentence-transformers model) or your own provider:

```python
grub("./docs", method="semantic", embed=my_openai_embedding_function)
```

### Long documents, chunking, and persistence

```python
grub("./book.txt", chunk=1500)  # split into passages, not whole files
grub("./src", extensions=[".py"])  # filter what gets indexed

from grub import Searcher

grub("./big_codebase").save("code.grub")  # build once
Searcher.load("code.grub")  # reload instantly
```

### From the command line

```bash
grub ./docs "how do I configure logging"
grub ./src --extensions .py --snippets "retry with backoff"
grub https://example.com/guide --semantic "getting started"
grub ./docs                                  # interactive prompt
```

### The legacy API still works

The original `SearchStore` and friends are unchanged and still exported,
so existing code keeps running:

```python
from grub import SearchStore

import sklearn, os

search = SearchStore(os.path.dirname(sklearn.__file__) + "/{}.py")
search("how to calibrate the estimates of my classifier")
```

---

## How it works

grub is a thin, honest pipeline:

```default
source ──to_store──▶ store ──backend──▶ scores ──▶ SearchResults
```

1. **`to_store`** turns any source into a `Mapping[str, str]`.
2. A **backend** (TF-IDF, embeddings, or a hybrid) scores every document
   against your query.
3. Results come back ranked, scored, and annotated with snippets.

Every stage is swappable — see the `grub-extend` skill or
[`grub/backends.py`](). That’s the whole trick: simple
things stay simple, powerful things stay possible.

## Install

```bash
pip install grub               # core (TF-IDF / lexical search)
pip install 'grub[semantic]'   # adds local embedding-based search
```

# _autosummary/grub.backends.html.md

# grub.backends

Search backends: the engines that score documents against a query.

Every backend implements the same tiny interface:

* `index(docs)` – build an index over a list of text documents.
* `scores(query)` – return a relevance score per document.
* `query(query, n)` – return the top-`n` `(indices, scores)`.

Three backends ship with grub:

* [`TfidfBackend`](_autosummary/grub.backends.html.md#grub.backends.TfidfBackend) – lexical TF-IDF + cosine similarity (default,
  no extra dependencies).
* [`SemanticBackend`](_autosummary/grub.backends.html.md#grub.backends.SemanticBackend) – dense embeddings; understands meaning, not
  just words. Needs `sentence-transformers` (`pip install grub[semantic]`)
  or any embedding function you supply.
* [`HybridBackend`](_autosummary/grub.backends.html.md#grub.backends.HybridBackend) – a weighted blend of the two.

Pick a backend by name with [`make_backend()`](_autosummary/grub.backends.html.md#grub.backends.make_backend).

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_SEMANTIC_MODEL`](_autosummary/grub.backends.html.md#grub.backends.DFLT_SEMANTIC_MODEL)   | Default sentence-transformers model for [`SemanticBackend`](_autosummary/grub.backends.html.md#grub.backends.SemanticBackend).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

A weighted blend of lexical (TF-IDF) and semantic search.

`alpha` is the lexical weight: `1.0` is pure TF-IDF, `0.0` is
pure semantic, `0.5` (default) gives an even mix.

Fast, dependency-light, and excellent when the query shares actual
words with the documents – the right default for code and docs.

### *class* grub.base.SearchStore(store, n_neighbors=10, tokenizer=<function camelcase_and_underscore_tokenizer>)

Bases: [`StoreMixin`](_autosummary/grub.base.html.md#grub.base.StoreMixin)

Build a search index for anything (that is given a mapping interface with string values).

A store is anything with a `collections.Mapping` interface.
Typically, a store’s backend comes from local files or data-base wrapped into a mapping
(see `py2store` for tools to do that!).
For testing purposes though, we’ll use a `dict` here:

```pycon
>>> store = {
... "Nelson Mandela": "The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall.",
... "Walt Disney": "The way to get started is to quit talking and begin doing.",
... "Steve Jobs": "Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life."
... }
>>> search = SearchStore(store, n_neighbors=2)  # our store is small, so need to restrict our result size to less
>>> list(search('living'))
['Steve Jobs', 'Nelson Mandela']
```

A `SearchStore` instance is picklable.

```pycon
>>> import pickle
>>> unserialized_search = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(search))
>>> list(unserialized_search('living'))
['Steve Jobs', 'Nelson Mandela']
```

# _autosummary/grub.cli.html.md

# grub.cli

Command-line interface for grub: `grub SOURCE [QUERY ...]`.

Search a folder, glob, module, or URL straight from the shell:

```default
grub ./docs "how do I configure logging"
grub ./src --extensions .py --snippets "retry with backoff"
grub https://example.com            # no query -> interactive prompt
```

Run `grub --help` for the full option list.

### Functions

| [`run`](_autosummary/grub.cli.html.md#grub.cli.run)(source, \*query[, method, n, snippets, ...])   | Search `source`; with no query, drop into an interactive prompt.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`main`](_autosummary/grub.cli.html.md#grub.cli.main)([argv])                                       | Entry point for the `grub` console script; returns its exit code.  |

### grub.cli.main(argv=None)

Entry point for the `grub` console script; returns its exit code.

`argv` defaults to `sys.argv[1:]`. `cw.dispatch()` takes it positionally and
reproduces the grammar this CLI has always had – pinned by `misc/cli_golden_py*.json`
and asserted by `tests/test_cli_parity.py`.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

### grub.cli.run(source, \*query, method='tfidf', n=10, snippets=False, semantic=False, hybrid=False, chunk=0, extensions='')

Search `source`; with no query, drop into an interactive prompt.

* **Parameters:**
  * **source** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – folder, glob, `dir/{}.ext` format, module path, or URL.
  * **query** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the search query (omit for an interactive session).
  * **method** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `tfidf`, `semantic`, or `hybrid`.
  * **n** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – number of results to show.
  * **snippets** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – also show the matching snippet for each result.
  * **semantic** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – shortcut for `--method semantic`.
  * **hybrid** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – shortcut for `--method hybrid`.
  * **chunk** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – split documents into windows of this many characters.
  * **extensions** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – comma-separated file extensions to restrict to,
    e.g. `.py,.md`.


# _autosummary/grub.facade.html.md

# grub.facade

The one-line front door to grub: [`grub()`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#module-grub) (and its alias [`search()`](_autosummary/grub.facade.html.md#grub.facade.search)).

`grub(source)` builds a reusable [`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher);
`grub(source, query)` searches in a single call. That is the whole
API most people ever need.

### Functions

| [`grub`](_autosummary/grub.facade.html.md#grub.facade.grub)(source[, query, method, n])       | Search *anything*, in one line.                                                                                            |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`search`](_autosummary/grub.facade.html.md#grub.facade.search)(source, query, \*[, method, n]) | Search `source` for `query` -- a query-first alias of [`grub()`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#module-grub). |

### grub.facade.grub(source, query=None, , method='tfidf', n=10, \*\*kwargs)

Search *anything*, in one line.

Point `grub` at a source – a folder, a glob, a Python module, a
URL, a dict, or a list of strings – and it builds a search engine.

Called with just a `source` it returns a reusable
[`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher):

```pycon
>>> docs = {
...     'python': 'Python is a popular programming language.',
...     'guitar': 'A guitar is a musical instrument with strings.',
...     'coffee': 'Coffee is a hot drink brewed from beans.',
... }
>>> searcher = grub(docs)
>>> searcher('a musical instrument').keys[0]
'guitar'
```

Called with a `query` too, it searches immediately and returns the
[`SearchResults`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#grub.results.SearchResults):

```pycon
>>> grub(docs, 'hot drink brewed from beans').keys[0]
'coffee'
```

* **Parameters:**
  * **source** – anything [`grub.sources.to_store()`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.to_store) understands.
    An existing [`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher) is reused as-is.
  * **query** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – if given, search for it and return results; otherwise
    return the searcher.
  * **method** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `'tfidf'`, `'semantic'`, or `'hybrid'`.
  * **n** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – number of results.
  * **kwargs** – forwarded to [`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher)
    (e.g. `chunk=1500`, `extensions=['.py']`, `embed=...`).

### grub.facade.search(source, query, , method='tfidf', n=10, \*\*kwargs)

Search `source` for `query` – a query-first alias of [`grub()`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#module-grub).

* **Return type:**
  [`SearchResults`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#grub.results.SearchResults)

```pycon
>>> search(['apple pie', 'car engine', 'apple orchard'], 'fruit apple').keys[0]
'0'
```


# _autosummary/grub.html.md

# grub

grub – a ridiculously simple search engine factory.

Point grub at *anything* – a folder, a Python package, a website, a
dict, a list of strings – and get back a search engine in one line:

```default
from grub import grub

search = grub('./my_docs')              # build a searcher
results = search('how do I configure logging')

for hit in results:
    print(hit.score, hit.key, hit.snippet)
```

Or search in a single call:

```default
grub('./my_docs', 'how do I configure logging')
```

Three search methods are available: `'tfidf'` (lexical, the default),
`'semantic'` (embeddings – `pip install grub[semantic]`), and
`'hybrid'` (a blend of both).

### Functions

| [`grub`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.grub)(source[, query, method, n])                   | Search *anything*, in one line.                                                                                |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`search`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.search)(source, query, \*[, method, n])             | Search `source` for `query` -- a query-first alias of [`grub()`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#module-grub). |
| [`to_store`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.to_store)(source, \*[, recursive, extensions, ...]) | Coerce `source` into a `Mapping[str, str]` ready to be searched.                                               |
| [`chunk_text`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.chunk_text)(text, \*[, size, overlap])              | Split `text` into overlapping character windows.                                                               |
| [`chunk_store`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.chunk_store)(store, \*[, size, overlap])            | Chunk every value of `store`; keys become `"{key}#{n}"`.                                                       |
| [`html_to_text`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.html_to_text)(html)                                 | Strip HTML tags, returning visible text only.                                                                  |
| [`make_backend`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.make_backend)([method, tokenizer, embed, ...])      | Build a backend by name: `'tfidf'`, `'semantic'`, or `'hybrid'`.                                               |
| [`grubber`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.grubber)(search_store[, n])                         | Computes a TF-IDF model and a KNN model for a search store.                                                    |

### *class* grub.SearchResults(results=(), , query=None)

Bases: [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

An ordered list of [`SearchResult`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.SearchResult), best match first.

It *is* a list, so it indexes, slices, and iterates as you’d expect:

```default
>>> results = SearchResults(
...     [SearchResult("guitar", 0.9, "a string instrument"),
...      SearchResult("piano", 0.4, "a keyboard instrument")],
...     query="instrument",
... )
>>> len(results)
2
>>> results[0].key
'guitar'
>>> results.keys
['guitar', 'piano']
>>> [round(s, 1) for s in results.scores]
[0.9, 0.4]
>>> results.as_dict()['guitar']
0.9
```

#### as_dict()

A `{key: score}` mapping of the results.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### *property* keys *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*

Just the keys, ranked best-first.

#### *property* scores *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*

Just the scores, ranked best-first.

#### show(, snippets=True)

A human-readable, multi-line rendering of the results.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### *property* snippets *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*

Just the snippets, ranked best-first.

### *class* grub.SearchStore(store, n_neighbors=10, tokenizer=<function camelcase_and_underscore_tokenizer>)

Bases: [`StoreMixin`](_autosummary/grub.base.html.md#grub.base.StoreMixin)

Build a search index for anything (that is given a mapping interface with string values).

A store is anything with a `collections.Mapping` interface.
Typically, a store’s backend comes from local files or data-base wrapped into a mapping
(see `py2store` for tools to do that!).
For testing purposes though, we’ll use a `dict` here:

```pycon
>>> store = {
... "Nelson Mandela": "The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall.",
... "Walt Disney": "The way to get started is to quit talking and begin doing.",
... "Steve Jobs": "Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life."
... }
>>> search = SearchStore(store, n_neighbors=2)  # our store is small, so need to restrict our result size to less
>>> list(search('living'))
['Steve Jobs', 'Nelson Mandela']
```

A `SearchStore` instance is picklable.

```pycon
>>> import pickle
>>> unserialized_search = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(search))
>>> list(unserialized_search('living'))
['Steve Jobs', 'Nelson Mandela']
```

### *class* grub.Searcher(source, \*, method='tfidf', n_results=10, tokenizer=<function camelcase_and_underscore_tokenizer>, embed=None, model='all-MiniLM-L6-v2', alpha=0.5, chunk=None, snippets=True, backend=None, \*\*source_kwargs)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Index any source and search it.

```pycon
>>> docs = {
...     'python': 'Python is a popular high level programming language.',
...     'guitar': 'A guitar is a musical instrument with six strings.',
...     'coffee': 'Coffee is a hot drink brewed from roasted beans.',
... }
>>> searcher = Searcher(docs)
>>> searcher
<Searcher: tfidf index over 3 documents>
>>> results = searcher('a musical instrument')
>>> results.keys[0]
'guitar'
>>> searcher('hot drink brewed from beans').keys[0]
'coffee'
```

Each result carries a score and a snippet explaining the match:

```pycon
>>> hit = results[0]
>>> hit.key
'guitar'
>>> hit.score > 0
True
>>> 'musical instrument' in hit.snippet
True
```

#### fit()

Build the search index. Called automatically on first search.

* **Return type:**


### grub.chunk_store(store, , size=1500, overlap=200)

Chunk every value of `store`; keys become `"{key}#{n}"`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

```pycon
>>> sorted(chunk_store({"doc": "abcdef"}, size=3, overlap=0))
['doc#0', 'doc#1']
```

### grub.chunk_text(text, , size=1500, overlap=200)

Split `text` into overlapping character windows.

Long documents search better in pieces: a hit then points at a
passage instead of a whole file.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

```pycon
>>> chunk_text("abcdefghij", size=4, overlap=1)
['abcd', 'defg', 'ghij', 'j']
>>> chunk_text("short", size=100)
['short']
```

### grub.grub(source, query=None, , method='tfidf', n=10, \*\*kwargs)

Search *anything*, in one line.

Point `grub` at a source – a folder, a glob, a Python module, a
URL, a dict, or a list of strings – and it builds a search engine.

Called with just a `source` it returns a reusable
[`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher):

```pycon
>>> docs = {
...     'python': 'Python is a popular programming language.',
...     'guitar': 'A guitar is a musical instrument with strings.',
...     'coffee': 'Coffee is a hot drink brewed from beans.',
... }
>>> searcher = grub(docs)
>>> searcher('a musical instrument').keys[0]
'guitar'
```

Called with a `query` too, it searches immediately and returns the
[`SearchResults`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#grub.results.SearchResults):

```pycon
>>> grub(docs, 'hot drink brewed from beans').keys[0]
'coffee'
```

* **Parameters:**
  * **source** – anything [`grub.sources.to_store()`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.to_store) understands.
    An existing [`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher) is reused as-is.
  * **query** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – if given, search for it and return results; otherwise
    return the searcher.
  * **method** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `'tfidf'`, `'semantic'`, or `'hybrid'`.
  * **n** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – number of results.
  * **kwargs** – forwarded to [`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher)
    (e.g. `chunk=1500`, `extensions=['.py']`, `embed=...`).

### grub.grubber(search_store, n=10)

Computes a TF-IDF model and a KNN model for a search store.

### grub.search_documented_attributes(obj, obj_to_attrs=<function ddir>, max_results=10)

Search the documented attributes of a python object

* **Parameters:**
  * **obj** – Any python object
  * **obj_to_attrs** – The function that gives you attribute names of an object.
* **Returns:**
  A SearchStore instance to search attributes via their docs

```pycon
>>> from inspect import getmodule
>>> containing_module = getmodule(search_documented_attributes)  # the module of this function
>>> search_module = search_documented_attributes(containing_module, max_results=3)
>>> list(search_module('documented attributes'))  # if you get an error here, it's probably just be that the docs changed
['search_documented_attributes', 'ddir', 'inspect']
>>> list(search_module('documented objects'))  # if you get an error here, it's probably just be that the docs changed
['search_documented_attributes', 'DocTestFinder', 'doctest_finder']
```

### grub.to_store(source, , recursive=True, extensions=None, chunk=None, encoding='utf-8', max_bytes=1000000)

Coerce `source` into a `Mapping[str, str]` ready to be searched.

`source` may be:

* a `Mapping` – used as-is
* a folder path – every (decodable) text file under it
* a glob pattern – every matching file
* a `"path/{}.ext"` format – a lazy `py2store` text store
* a Python module/package – its `.py` source files
* a URL (or list of URLs) – fetched and stripped to text
* a list of strings – enumerated into `{"0": ..., "1": ...}`
* an iterable of `(key, value)` pairs – turned into a dict

```pycon
>>> store = to_store({"a": "first doc", "b": "second doc"})
>>> dict(store)
{'a': 'first doc', 'b': 'second doc'}
>>> sorted(to_store(["red", "green", "blue"]))
['0', '1', '2']
```

* **Parameters:**
  * **recursive** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – walk sub-directories (folder sources only).
  * **extensions** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – keep only files with these extensions, e.g. `[".py"]`.
  * **chunk** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – split values into overlapping windows – an int size or a
    `(size, overlap)` pair. Handy for long documents.
  * **encoding** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – text encoding for files.
  * **max_bytes** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – skip files larger than this (folder/glob sources).
* **Return type:**
  [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

# _autosummary/grub.results.html.md

# grub.results

Rich search results: keys, scores, and snippets that explain a match.

Where the legacy [`grub.SearchStore`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.SearchStore) returns a bare array of keys,
the modern [`grub.Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.Searcher) returns a [`SearchResults`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#grub.results.SearchResults) – a
list of [`SearchResult`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#grub.results.SearchResult) records that also know their score and a
snippet showing *why* the document matched.

### Classes

| [`SearchResult`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#grub.results.SearchResult)(key, score[, snippet])   | A single hit.                                                                                       |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SearchResults`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#grub.results.SearchResults)([results, query])       | An ordered list of [`SearchResult`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#grub.results.SearchResult), best match first. |

### *class* grub.results.SearchResult(key, score, snippet='')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A single hit.

* **Parameters:**
  * **key** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the document’s key in the store.
  * **score** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – relevance in `[0, 1]` (higher is better).
  * **snippet** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – a short excerpt showing why the document matched.

### *class* grub.results.SearchResults(results=(), , query=None)

Bases: [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

An ordered list of [`SearchResult`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#grub.results.SearchResult), best match first.

It *is* a list, so it indexes, slices, and iterates as you’d expect:

```default
>>> results = SearchResults(
...     [SearchResult("guitar", 0.9, "a string instrument"),
...      SearchResult("piano", 0.4, "a keyboard instrument")],
...     query="instrument",
... )
>>> len(results)
2
>>> results[0].key
'guitar'
>>> results.keys
['guitar', 'piano']
>>> [round(s, 1) for s in results.scores]
[0.9, 0.4]
>>> results.as_dict()['guitar']
0.9
```

#### as_dict()

A `{key: score}` mapping of the results.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### *property* keys *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*

Just the keys, ranked best-first.

#### *property* scores *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*

Just the scores, ranked best-first.

#### show(, snippets=True)

A human-readable, multi-line rendering of the results.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### *property* snippets *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)*

Just the snippets, ranked best-first.


# _autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md

# grub.searcher

The [`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher) – grub’s unified, modern search object.

A [`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher) wraps three things behind one friendly interface:

* a **store** (any source, via [`grub.sources.to_store()`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.to_store)),
* a **backend** (TF-IDF, semantic, or hybrid, via [`grub.backends`](_autosummary/grub.backends.html.md#module-grub.backends)),
* **results** enriched with scores and snippets ([`grub.results`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#module-grub.results)).

You rarely build one by hand – [`grub.grub()`](_autosummary/grub.html.md#grub.grub) is the front door –
but the class is here when you want full control, persistence, or to
plug in your own backend.

### Classes

| [`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher)(source, \*[, method, n_results, ...])   | Index any source and search it.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|

### *class* grub.searcher.Searcher(source, \*, method='tfidf', n_results=10, tokenizer=<function camelcase_and_underscore_tokenizer>, embed=None, model='all-MiniLM-L6-v2', alpha=0.5, chunk=None, snippets=True, backend=None, \*\*source_kwargs)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Index any source and search it.

```pycon
>>> docs = {
...     'python': 'Python is a popular high level programming language.',
...     'guitar': 'A guitar is a musical instrument with six strings.',
...     'coffee': 'Coffee is a hot drink brewed from roasted beans.',
... }
>>> searcher = Searcher(docs)
>>> searcher
<Searcher: tfidf index over 3 documents>
>>> results = searcher('a musical instrument')
>>> results.keys[0]
'guitar'
>>> searcher('hot drink brewed from beans').keys[0]
'coffee'
```

Each result carries a score and a snippet explaining the match:

```pycon
>>> hit = results[0]
>>> hit.key
'guitar'
>>> hit.score > 0
True
>>> 'musical instrument' in hit.snippet
True
```

#### fit()

Build the search index. Called automatically on first search.

* **Return type:**
  [`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher)

#### *property* is_fitted *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

Whether the index has been built.

#### *classmethod* load(path)

Load a searcher previously written by [`save()`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher.save).

* **Return type:**
  [`Searcher`](_autosummary/grub.searcher.html.md#grub.searcher.Searcher)

#### save(path)

Pickle this searcher (index included) to `path`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
* **Returns:**
  the path written to.

#### search(query, n=None)

Return the [`SearchResults`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#grub.results.SearchResults) for `query`.

* **Return type:**
  [`SearchResults`](_autosummary/grub.results.html.md#grub.results.SearchResults)


# _autosummary/grub.sources.html.md

# grub.sources

Source adapters: turn *anything* into a searchable store.

A “store” here is just a `Mapping` whose values are text. Everything
grub can search – a folder, a glob, a Python package, a website, a list
of strings, a plain dict – is funnelled through [`to_store()`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.to_store), which
detects the kind of source and returns a uniform mapping.

The single entry point is [`to_store()`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.to_store). The `from_*` helpers are
there when you want to be explicit.

### Functions

| [`to_store`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.to_store)(source, \*[, recursive, extensions, ...])   | Coerce `source` into a `Mapping[str, str]` ready to be searched.     |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`from_dir`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.from_dir)(directory, \*[, recursive, ...])            | Every decodable text file under `directory`, keyed by relative path. |
| [`from_files`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.from_files)(paths, \*[, encoding])                    | Read the given files into a `{name: content}` dict.                  |
| [`from_module`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.from_module)(module)                                  | The `.py` source files of a Python module or package.                |
| [`from_strings`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.from_strings)(strings)                                | Enumerate strings into a `{index: string}` dict.                     |
| [`from_urls`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.from_urls)(urls, \*[, encoding, timeout])             | Fetch URLs and return `{url: text}` with HTML stripped to text.      |
| [`chunk_text`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.chunk_text)(text, \*[, size, overlap])                | Split `text` into overlapping character windows.                     |
| [`chunk_store`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.chunk_store)(store, \*[, size, overlap])              | Chunk every value of `store`; keys become `"{key}#{n}"`.             |
| [`html_to_text`](_autosummary/grub.sources.html.md#grub.sources.html_to_text)(html)                                   | Strip HTML tags, returning visible text only.                        |

### grub.sources.chunk_store(store, , size=1500, overlap=200)

Chunk every value of `store`; keys become `"{key}#{n}"`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

```pycon
>>> sorted(chunk_store({"doc": "abcdef"}, size=3, overlap=0))
['doc#0', 'doc#1']
```

### grub.sources.chunk_text(text, , size=1500, overlap=200)

Split `text` into overlapping character windows.

Long documents search better in pieces: a hit then points at a
passage instead of a whole file.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

```pycon
>>> chunk_text("abcdefghij", size=4, overlap=1)
['abcd', 'defg', 'ghij', 'j']
>>> chunk_text("short", size=100)
['short']
```

### grub.sources.from_dir(directory, , recursive=True, extensions=None, encoding='utf-8', max_bytes=1000000, skip_dirs=frozenset({'.eggs', '.git', '.hg', '.idea', '.mypy_cache', '.pytest_cache', '.ruff_cache', '.svn', '.venv', '.vscode', '_\_pycache_\_', 'build', 'dist', 'node_modules', 'venv'}))

Every decodable text file under `directory`, keyed by relative path.

Binary files, oversized files, and noise directories (`.git`,
`__pycache__`, `node_modules`, …) are skipped automatically.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### grub.sources.from_files(paths, , encoding='utf-8')

Read the given files into a `{name: content}` dict.

Keys are file names; if names collide the relative path is used.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### grub.sources.from_module(module)

The `.py` source files of a Python module or package.

* **Return type:**
  [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

### grub.sources.from_strings(strings)

Enumerate strings into a `{index: string}` dict.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

```pycon
>>> from_strings(["alpha", "beta"])
{'0': 'alpha', '1': 'beta'}
```

### grub.sources.from_urls(urls, , encoding='utf-8', timeout=30.0)

Fetch URLs and return `{url: text}` with HTML stripped to text.

Uses only the standard library. Unreachable URLs are skipped.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### grub.sources.html_to_text(html)

Strip HTML tags, returning visible text only.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> html_to_text("<h1>Title</h1><p>Hello <b>world</b></p>")
'Title Hello world'
>>> html_to_text("<style>.x{}</style><p>visible</p>")
'visible'
```

### grub.sources.to_store(source, , recursive=True, extensions=None, chunk=None, encoding='utf-8', max_bytes=1000000)

Coerce `source` into a `Mapping[str, str]` ready to be searched.

`source` may be:

* a `Mapping` – used as-is
* a folder path – every (decodable) text file under it
* a glob pattern – every matching file
* a `"path/{}.ext"` format – a lazy `py2store` text store
* a Python module/package – its `.py` source files
* a URL (or list of URLs) – fetched and stripped to text
* a list of strings – enumerated into `{"0": ..., "1": ...}`
* an iterable of `(key, value)` pairs – turned into a dict

```pycon
>>> store = to_store({"a": "first doc", "b": "second doc"})
>>> dict(store)
{'a': 'first doc', 'b': 'second doc'}
>>> sorted(to_store(["red", "green", "blue"]))
['0', '1', '2']
```

* **Parameters:**
  * **recursive** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – walk sub-directories (folder sources only).
  * **extensions** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – keep only files with these extensions, e.g. `[".py"]`.
  * **chunk** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – split values into overlapping windows – an int size or a
    `(size, overlap)` pair. Handy for long documents.
  * **encoding** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – text encoding for files.
  * **max_bytes** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – skip files larger than this (folder/glob sources).
* **Return type:**
  [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)


# _autosummary/grub.util.html.md

# grub.util

Small shared utilities for grub: tokenizing, clamping, snippet extraction.

These are low-level helpers used across grub’s modules. They have no
heavy dependencies and are safe to import anywhere.

### Functions

| [`simple_tokenizer`](_autosummary/grub.util.html.md#grub.util.simple_tokenizer)(text)                            | Lower-cased word tokens of a string.                              |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`clamp_n`](_autosummary/grub.util.html.md#grub.util.clamp_n)(n, size)                                  | Clamp a requested result count to `[1, size]`.                    |
| [`best_snippet`](_autosummary/grub.util.html.md#grub.util.best_snippet)(text, query, \*[, width, tokenizer]) | Return a short excerpt of `text` that best matches `query`.       |
| [`is_url`](_autosummary/grub.util.html.md#grub.util.is_url)(value)                                     | Whether `value` looks like a fetchable URL.                       |
| [`truncate`](_autosummary/grub.util.html.md#grub.util.truncate)(text[, width])                           | Collapse whitespace and truncate `text` to at most `width` chars. |

### grub.util.best_snippet(text, query, \*, width=240, tokenizer=<function simple_tokenizer>)

Return a short excerpt of `text` that best matches `query`.

The excerpt is the single line sharing the most tokens with the
query – a cheap way to show *why* a document matched.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> doc = "Intro line.\nThe quick brown fox jumps over.\nTrailing words."
>>> best_snippet(doc, "quick brown fox")
'The quick brown fox jumps over.'
```

With no overlap at all it falls back to the start of the text:

```pycon
>>> best_snippet("alpha beta gamma", "nothing matches here", width=80)
'alpha beta gamma'
```

### grub.util.clamp_n(n, size)

Clamp a requested result count to `[1, size]`.

Search backends choke when asked for more neighbours than they have
documents; this keeps requests in range.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

```pycon
>>> clamp_n(10, 3)
3
>>> clamp_n(5, 100)
5
>>> clamp_n(0, 100)
1
```

### grub.util.is_url(value)

Whether `value` looks like a fetchable URL.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

```pycon
>>> is_url("https://example.com")
True
>>> is_url("./local/path")
False
```

### grub.util.simple_tokenizer(text)

Lower-cased word tokens of a string.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

```pycon
>>> simple_tokenizer("Hello, World! Version 2")
['hello', 'world', 'version', '2']
```

### grub.util.truncate(text, width=240)

Collapse whitespace and truncate `text` to at most `width` chars.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> truncate("  lots   of   space  ", width=80)
'lots of space'
>>> truncate("abcdefghij", width=5)
'abcd…'
```

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`grub` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `grub-extend`

Use when extending or customizing grub — plugging in a custom embedding function or provider (OpenAI, Cohere, Voyage, a local model), writing a new search backend, adding a source adapter, or tuning the tokenizer / TF-IDF parameters. Triggers on “use OpenAI embeddings with grub”, “custom embeddings for grub”, “add a backend to grub”, “grub custom source”, “make grub search <some new thing>”.

Source: [`.claude/skills/grub-extend`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/grub/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/grub-extend).

### `grub-search`

Use when searching a body of text with grub — pointing it at a folder, a codebase, a Python module/package, a set of docs, a website, or a list of strings, then querying it. Triggers on “search my docs/code/notes”, “find where X is mentioned”, “build a search index”, “which file talks about Y”, “semantic search over these files”, “grub search”, or running the grub CLI.

Source: [`.claude/skills/grub-search`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/grub/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/grub-search).

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/grub/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`grub.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/grub/grub.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/grub/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
